TURNOVER TAX RULES, 19516
TURNOVER TAX RULES, 1996
(Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary,
Part II, 1st July, 1996)
S.R.O. 552(1)/96, dated 1‑7‑1996.‑‑In
exercise of the powers conferred by section 50 of the Sales Tax Act, 1990, read
with sections 3‑A and 26‑A thereof, the Central Board of Revenue is
pleased to make the following rules, namely:‑‑
1. Short title, application and
commencement.‑‑(1)
These Rules may be called Turnover Tax Rules, 1996.
(2) These shall apply to the persons
making taxable supplies whose taxable turnover does not exceed one million
rupees any time during the last twelve months.
(3) These shall come into force on
and from the first day of July, 1996.
2. Definitions.‑‑(1) For the purposes
of these Rules,‑‑‑
"Act" means the Sales Tax
Act, 1990;
"Annex" means an annex
appended to these Rules.
"enrolment application"
means application for enrolment of turnover taxpayers in the form at Annex‑A;
"enrolment certificate"
means a certificate of enrolment as at Annex‑B; and
"return" means turnover
tax return‑cum‑payment challan as in form at Annex‑C.
(2) All other terms and expressions
used but not defined in these Rules shall have the same meaning as are assigned
to them under the Act.
3. Enrolment of turnover taxpayer.‑‑(1) A person whose
taxable turnover does not exceed one million rupees shall make an enrolment
application to the Collector having jurisdiction in the area where his business
premises are located.
(2) The Collector shall, having
satisfied himself with the requisite information provided' in the enrolment
application cause the applicant to be enroled and issue ‑the enrolment
certificate accordingly.
4. Payment of turnover tax.‑‑(1) A person required
to 0y turnover tax shall file the return in triplicate under section 26‑A
of the Act in the designated bank alongwith the amount of turnover tax due as
indicated in column 04 of the return.
(2) The Bank official shall ensure
that the particulars entered in all the three copies of the return are
identical and that the amount deposited by the turnover taxpayer tallies with
the amount indicated as "turnover tax due" in the return and shall
thereafter sign and stamp the return indicating the date of payment of tax and
submission of tax return.
(3) The Bank shall forward the
original copy of the return to the Collectorate and the duplicate shall be
delivered to the turnover taxpayer as a receipt of payment of turnover tax and
filing of return and the third copy shall be retained by the Bank for its
record.
(4) In case of payment through
cheque, pay order or bank draft, the Bank will receive the return in triplicate
alongwith the instrument of payment for the amount of tax due indicated in the
return and issue a provisional acknowledgement receipt to the registered
person.
(5) On clearance of the instrument,
the Bank official shall sign and stamp the return indicating the date on which
the payment is received by the Bank and the said date shall be treated as the
date of payment of tax and submission of tax return.
5. Records to be kept.‑‑A person required to
pay turnover tax under section 3‑A shall keep the following records
namely,‑‑
(i)Record of purchases indicating
description, quantity and value of goods purchased and the name and address of
the seller.
(ii) Record of sales indicating
description, quantity and value of goods sold, name and address of the buyer.
